sources: https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state-forests/forest.html?id=sft00012 (Chengwatana State Forest page; its facility data from https://maps.dnr.state.mn.us/cgi-bin/compass/feature_detail.cgi?id=sft00012, last_updated 2026-07-02: Snake River Campground cmp00008), read 2026-11-11

sites.source: DNR feature data for cmp00008 Snake River Campground: 'drive_in_campsites': 26 (2 accessible), last_updated 2026-07-02; the facility map numbers sites 1-26

hookups.source: DNR cmp00008: 'The campground is considered "primitive" ... The campsites consist of a cleared area, fire ring, and table'; state forest camping FAQ: 'there are no utilities such as electricity or sewer available at the campsites', read 2026-11-11

facilities.source: DNR cmp00008: 'vault toilets, garbage cans, and drinking water are available' (1 well, 1 toilet building on the facility map); state forest camping FAQ: 'State forest campgrounds do not have dump stations.', read 2026-11-11

season.source: https://files.dnr.state.mn.us/maps/state_forests/cmp00008.pdf: 'Closed in winter months.'; state forest camping FAQ: 'State forest campgrounds are open seasonally. Spring opening dates and fall closing dates vary by campground'

values.note: Paid on arrival or by same-day advance payment online. The 14-night limit runs from the first Saturday in May to the second Sunday in September; 21 nights the rest of the year.

booking.source: https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state-forests/camping.html: 'Individual campsites do not accept reservations; they are available by same day advance payment.'; 'limited to a total of 14 days in any one forest campground between the first Saturday in May through the second Sunday in September, or 21 days the rest of the year', read 2026-11-11

note: Primitive campground among tall pines along the Snake River in Chengwatana State Forest, managed by Wild River State Park; medium ~30-ft RVs fit, larger rigs struggle on the loop road. Open ~May 1 to end of deer season. ATVs are not allowed in the campground. --Claude
summary: DNR forest page data (updated 2026-07-02), facility map and state forest FAQ read: 26 drive-in primitive sites, no hookups, vault toilets, drinking water, no dump, no reservations (same-day payment), 14-night limit in season, closed in winter. $17 fee (stored) stands; the 30-ft max length and the May-to-deer-season dates are on no DNR page read (kept as unconfirmed). Not waterfront confirmed. Website to the hyphen URL form.

OHV: Chengwatana State Forest has OHV trails and the Matthew Lourey State Trail passes south of the campground, but the DNR says 'ATV use is not allowed in the campground'; a general campground, not a staging area. No action.
